issues.title: agentHost: load named host tools when no client can run tool search (#340101)
issues.body:
* agentHost: rank deferred tools on the host when no client can run tool search

Tool search is a client tool, but the tools it gates include server and MCP
tools that the host runs itself. When the client that runs the search is gone,
e.g. an autonomous Agent Merge turn after the window closed, the search failed
with "No client was connected to run Search tools" and no deferred tool could
be loaded for the rest of the turn.

Rank the same deferred-tool corpus on the host in that case: tools named in
the query first, then tf-idf over names and descriptions.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <redacted@example.com>

* agentHost: load exactly named host tools when tool search has no client

Replace the tf-idf ranking fallback with exact-name matching. Client tools
are left out because they cannot run without a client, and the result tells
the model why. When nothing matches, it lists the loadable names so the
model can search again by name.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <redacted@example.com>

* agentHost: answer tool search on the host when its client leaves mid-search

A search already routed to a client failed with "Client ... disconnected
before completing Search tools" when that client left before answering, so
no deferred tool could load. The override now answers on the host once the
client result has failed and no client can run tool search any more.

Also drops comments that restate the code.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <redacted@example.com>

* agentHost: keep the disconnect failure for a tool search already routed to a client

Agent Host publishes a failed completion for a routed search when its
client leaves, and chat state ignores any later completion. Answering that
call on the host gave the model tool references for a search the chat
shows as failed. The failure is now returned unchanged; the next search has
no client and takes the host fallback.

issues.body:
* agentHost: add agent title review strategy

Add an experiment-controlled `deferredAgentReview` title strategy behind
`chat.agentHost.experimental.agentTitleReview`. It keeps deferred host
naming, keeps `rename_chat` deferred with its `automatic` argument, and
adds a soft reminder with the current title after the first-response
refinement so the active agent renames only when the title is inaccurate
or no longer reflects the user's goal.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <redacted@example.com>

* agentHost: tighten agent title review reminder gating

- Gate the review reminder on the first response since the seed having
  completed rather than on refinement having started, so it also lifts
  when refinement never starts and never fires on the first turn of an
  auto-titled chat without a seed.
- Withhold the reminder while a host refinement is still in flight so
  the agent never judges the unrefined seed.
- Offer the reminder on at most three turns per chat, checked before the
  title-source metadata read.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <redacted@example.com>

* agentHost: consolidate title generation settings into one strategy setting

Replace the boolean `activeAgentTitleGeneration`, `deferredTitleGeneration`
and `agentTitleReview` settings with a single experiment-controlled enum,
`chat.agentHost.experimental.titleGeneration`, whose value is the strategy
(`utility`, `activeAgent`, `deferred` or `deferredAgentReview`). Arms are
now mutually exclusive and the treatment value matches the
`titleGenerationStrategy` telemetry value.

- The default keeps today's behavior: `activeAgent` outside Stable and
  `utility` in Stable.
- User values of the two shipped boolean settings are migrated to the new
  setting.
- The host prefers the `titleGeneration` root key and still reads the two
  legacy boolean root keys for clients that predate it.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <redacted@example.com>

* agentHost: ask the agent to rename at the end of its answer in title review

The review reminder did not say when to rename, and in practice the agent
renamed in a separate step before answering, delaying the answer on that
turn. Ask it to write the answer first and make the `rename_chat` call at
the end of the same message.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <redacted@example.com>

* agentHost: reduce the title setting to three strategies

`chat.agentHost.experimental.titleGeneration` now offers `utility`,
`activeAgent` and `agentReview` (previously `deferredAgentReview`, never
shipped), named by who writes the title.

- `deferred` (deferred host naming without agent review) is no longer
  selectable. It remains for sessions that already persisted it and for
  older clients that send the legacy boolean root key, so its stored
  meaning does not change.
- A legacy `deferredTitleGeneration: true` user value migrates to
  `agentReview`.
- The active agent naming reminder also asks the agent not to spend a
  separate step on renaming before it responds.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <redacted@example.com>

* agentHost: gate title review on a completed response and keep reminder cap across peer transition

Co-authored-by: Copilot <redacted@example.com>

  hosts that persist root config follow the current setting instead of a
  stale stored value. Adds an optional `derivedKeys` mapping to agent host
  configuration sync.
- Withhold the review reminder while a refinement started before a peer
  made the default chat independent is still keyed by the session.
- Let any finished first response satisfy the review gate: a cancelled or

Co-authored-by: Copilot <redacted@example.com>

* agentHost: let older clients supersede a persisted title strategy

A legacy-only root-config patch that changes activeAgentTitleGeneration or

issues.title: Keep all Agent Host shell output scrollable in the inline chat terminal (#340234)
issues.body:
* agentHost: Append shell output chunks instead of rolling snapshots

Once a Copilot shell command passes the 8 KiB large-output threshold, its
tool.execution_partial_result snapshots only carry the last 128 characters
of output. The Agent Host stitched those snapshots into the tool call's
terminal and cleared the whole transcript whenever a new tail did not
overlap the previous one, so long-running background shells showed a
single fragment of their latest line.

Subscribe to the SDK's append-only tool.shell_output event and append each
chunk instead, ignoring the call's snapshots once its first chunk arrives.
Also let the Background Shells preview re-wrap the line holding the cursor
when it narrows, as chat tool cards already do, so that line is no longer
clipped.

* Keep all retained background shell output scrollable

The Background Shells preview used the terminal.integrated.scrollback
setting (1,000 rows by default), so long output lost its oldest rows
while the preview was open, and the view jumped when scrolled up.

Let detached terminals override scrollback, keeping the override across
configuration updates, and have the preview keep as many rows as the
Agent Host keeps characters for a terminal. Every row holds at least one
character, so everything the host retains stays scrollable. The host's
100,000-character limit moves to a common module so both use one value.

* Hold back escape sequences that span shell output chunks

Each tool.shell_output chunk was stripped of ANSI escapes on its own, so
an escape sequence split by a chunk boundary leaked into the plain-text
terminal. Hold back an incomplete sequence at the end of a chunk, per
stream, until that stream's next chunk completes it. Cap what is held
back, so a sequence that never completes cannot hold back output.

Also treat only a line feed as ending a line. After a bare carriage
return the line is still open, so output from another stream now starts
on a new line instead of overwriting it.

* Type the chunk state before reading it

Assign the chunk state explicitly instead of through ??=, whose result type is a union with the new object literal and rejects reading openLineStream.

* Keep all Agent Host output scrollable in the inline chat terminal

The inline chat terminal of an Agent Host output-only shell kept only
terminal.integrated.scrollback rows (1,000 by default). Scrolled up
while output streamed, its oldest rows dropped under the view, so it
jumped or looked stuck, and the start of the output was unreachable.

Give it the same scrollback as the Background Shells preview: the Agent
Host's terminal content limit, so everything the host keeps stays
scrollable. Other chat terminal mirrors keep the setting.

issues.title: Fix truncated and unscrollable output in the Background Shells preview (#340222)
issues.body:
* agentHost: Append shell output chunks instead of rolling snapshots

Once a Copilot shell command passes the 8 KiB large-output threshold, its
tool.execution_partial_result snapshots only carry the last 128 characters
of output. The Agent Host stitched those snapshots into the tool call's
terminal and cleared the whole transcript whenever a new tail did not
overlap the previous one, so long-running background shells showed a
single fragment of their latest line.

Subscribe to the SDK's append-only tool.shell_output event and append each
chunk instead, ignoring the call's snapshots once its first chunk arrives.
Also let the Background Shells preview re-wrap the line holding the cursor
when it narrows, as chat tool cards already do, so that line is no longer
clipped.

* Keep all retained background shell output scrollable

The Background Shells preview used the terminal.integrated.scrollback
setting (1,000 rows by default), so long output lost its oldest rows
while the preview was open, and the view jumped when scrolled up.

Let detached terminals override scrollback, keeping the override across
configuration updates, and have the preview keep as many rows as the
Agent Host keeps characters for a terminal. Every row holds at least one
character, so everything the host retains stays scrollable. The host's
100,000-character limit moves to a common module so both use one value.

* Hold back escape sequences that span shell output chunks

Each tool.shell_output chunk was stripped of ANSI escapes on its own, so
an escape sequence split by a chunk boundary leaked into the plain-text
terminal. Hold back an incomplete sequence at the end of a chunk, per
stream, until that stream's next chunk completes it. Cap what is held
back, so a sequence that never completes cannot hold back output.

Also treat only a line feed as ending a line. After a bare carriage
return the line is still open, so output from another stream now starts
on a new line instead of overwriting it.

* Type the chunk state before reading it

Assign the chunk state explicitly instead of through ??=, whose result type is a union with the new object literal and rejects reading openLineStream.

issues.title: sessions: mount pill row before data in chat input toolbar fixtures (#340092)
issues.body:
`SessionChatPills_HorizontalOverflow` flaked about once every 25-60 renders
with the horizontal scrollbar of the overflowing pill row still visible.

`renderPills` set the session data before attaching the row and sized the
container last. The non-compact row's synchronous `scanDomNode()` therefore
ran while detached, and its first real measurement came from a native
`ResizeObserver`. That measurement reveals the auto-hiding scrollbar and
schedules a 500 ms hide. When the observer fired after the virtual-time
window, the hide ran on real timers and the screenshot caught the scrollbar.

Size the container and mount the row before setting data. The row then
measures its overflow synchronously, its reveal and hide run on virtual time,
and the later observer callback is a no-op.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <redacted@example.com>
